analysis: Chloroquine is primarily used for its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. It is well-established in the treatment of discoid lupus erythematosus, where it helps manage symptoms and reduce flare-ups. While chloroquine has some immunomodulatory effects that could theoretically benefit rheumatoid arthritis, it is not a standard or widely accepted treatment for this condition, as more effective and targeted therapies are available. Regarding infectious mononucleosis, chloroquine does not have a role, as this condition is caused by the Epstein-Barr virus, and chloroquine's antiviral properties are not effective against it. Therefore, based on the consensus and available evidence, chloroquine is primarily useful in treating discoid lupus erythematosus.
